title: Human-like autonomy emerges from self-play and a pinch of human data
abstract: arXiv:2606.19370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning has recently emerged as a way to train driving policies without any human data. It uses cheap, large-scale simulations to substitute expensive, large-scale human driving demonstrations. A key limitation of this approach is that policies trained through pure self-play can learn effective but alien driving conventions incompatible with people. Previous works attempt to mitigate such behavioral misalignments through extensive reward engineering and domain randomization, which are brittle and labor-intensive. Instead of completely discarding human demonstrations, our method treats them as a regularization objective on top of a minimal safe goal-reaching reward. Like the spice in a good stew, we find that a little human data goes a long way: our method uses only 30 minutes of human demonstrations, 2500x fewer than comparable imitation learning approaches. Resulting policies coordinate with held-out h

translated_title: 类人自动驾驶能力源于自我博弈与少量人类数据
translated_abstract: 自我博弈强化学习近来成为一种无需任何人类数据即可训练驾驶策略的方法。它利用廉价的大规模仿真来替代昂贵的大规模人类驾驶示范数据。该方法的一个关键局限在于，通过纯自我博弈训练的策略可能学到有效但与人类驾驶习惯不相容的“异类”驾驶惯例。先前的工作试图通过大量的奖励工程和域随机化来缓解这种行为失配问题，但这些方法既脆弱又耗费人力。我们的方法没有完全摒弃人类示范数据，而是将其作为一种正则化目标，叠加在最小化的安全到达目标奖励之上。就像好炖菜里的一点调味料，我们发现少量人类数据就能发挥巨大作用：我们的方法仅使用30分钟的人类驾驶示范，比同类的模仿学习方法少2500倍。所得到的策略能够与留出的人类驾驶行为（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将仅30分钟的人类驾驶示范作为自我博弈强化学习之上的正则化目标，以比模仿学习少2500倍的数据量训练出能与人类自然协调的类人自动驾驶策略。
en_tdlr: By treating just 30 minutes of human demonstrations as a regularization objective on top of self-play reinforcement learning, this paper trains human-like driving policies that coordinate naturally with humans while using 2500x less data than imitation learning.
